# America’s Governors

States and territories are where innovative ideas and policies are born, and successful policies become beacons of inspiration, demonstrating the power of local solutions to national challenges. America’s Governors are the architects of these policies and the custodians of our diverse and vibrant culture.

The National Governors Association provides informative gubernatorial resources, including current Governors’ biographies and terms in office, [First Spouse biographies](https://www.nga.org/governors/spouses/), [former Governors’ biographies](https://www.nga.org/former-governors/), [Governors’ staff contact information](https://www.nga.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Governors-State-Federal-Affairs-Representatives.pdf) and [social media](https://www.nga.org/governors/social/).

# Record Number of Women Ascend to Governors Offices

## The 2022 midterms were a record-breaking year for women candidates. Several states already have made history with electing their first-time female governor and some are yet to be decided as votes are still being tallied.

Nov. 13, 2022•

Barbara Rodriguez, The 19th

_Editor's Note: This article was originally published by [The 19th](https://19thnews.org/2022/05/governors-races-election-2022/)._  
  
At least 11 women are poised to win governorships following Tuesday’s election, a record number. Up until Tuesday, only nine women had served as governor at the same time. Just 45 women have served as governor in American history. But that will change, pending two races in Arizona and Oregon that have only women candidates.  
  
Twenty-five women had been on the ballot Election Day as major-party nominees in 36 governor’s races, another record.  
  
[Maura Healey has won](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/maura-healey-massachusetts-governor/) in Massachusetts, Decision Desk HQ projects, and will be the first out lesbian governor in U.S. history. A number of women Democrats won reelection in competitive races, including [Michigan’s Gretchen Whitmer](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/gretchen-whitmer-michigan-governor-reelection/)and [Kansas’ Laura Kelly](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/laura-kelly-kansas-governor-reelection/).  
  
Here are live results for 14 key governor’s races _The 19th_ is watching:  
  

### Alabama

  
Republican Gov. Kay Ivey, the first woman elected governor of Alabama, won a second four-year term, beating Democrat Yolanda Flowers. Flowers is the first Black woman in the state to win a major party’s nomination for governor. Ivey outraised Flowers throughout the election cycle.  
  
In a campaign ad released in the spring, Ivey claimed “blue state liberals” and others “stole” the 2020 election from Trump. She later told [television station WVTM 13](https://www.wvtm13.com/article/secretary-of-state-said-there-was-no-fraud-in-alabama-s-2020-general-election/39696085#) that she believes Trump won the election.  
  

### Arizona

  
Democrat Katie Hobbs and Republican Kari Lake are in a tight race for an open seat in one of the most closely watched governor’s races in the country.  
  
Hobbs, the current secretary of state, has staked her campaign on protecting elections and democracy. Lake, a former local television anchor, has never been elected to office and has made election denialism a key issue for her campaign. Lake has called [the 2020 election “stolen” and Biden an “illegitimate president.”](https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-biden-doug-ducey-arizona-donald-trump-710d8d35d6414784255fa133e08f190e) If she is elected, she would help oversee elections in a battleground state that is expected to have an outsize role in the 2024 presidential election.  
  

### Arkansas

  
Republican [Sarah Huckabee Sanders has won](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/sarah-huckabee-sanders-arkansas-governor/), Decision Desk HQ projects, making her the first woman to be elected governor of Arkansas.  
  
Sanders has never been elected to office, but she’s gained name recognition as a former White House press secretary for Trump and as the daughter of former Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee.  
  
Sanders, who has highlighted her ties to Trump’s administration on the campaign trail, has expressed some doubt about the 2020 election. She told the [Texarkana Gazette](https://www.texarkanagazette.com/news/2022/may/02/in-race-for-arkansas-governor-gop-hopefuls-differ/) ahead of the May primary: “I don't think we’ll ever know the depths of how much fraud existed.” If Leslie Rutledge — the state’s current attorney general and the Republican nominee for lieutenant governor — is elected alongside Sanders, the two would be among the first women in the country to serve together in the top posts.  
  

### Georgia

  
Democrat Stacey Abrams has lost to incumbent Republican Gov. Brian Kemp, Decision Desk HQ projects. Georgia has also never elected a woman governor.  
  
Abrams emphasized the importance of voting access in her second bid for governor and spent time on the trail highlighting issues including abortion, health care and economic inequality.  
  
Kemp is among the most prominent Republicans to dismiss Trump’s claims about problems with the 2020 election. Abrams has criticized Kemp’s [policies around voting](https://19thnews.org/2022/09/georgia-elections-voter-challenges/), which voting rights groups warn could make it harder for some people to vote.  
  
Abrams [refused to concede](https://19thnews.org/2022/09/stacey-abrams-trump-democracy-big-lie/) after her 2018 loss, claiming that Kemp suppressed voter turnout. Kemp denies this, and in October a judge [tossed a related lawsuit](https://www.axios.com/2022/09/30/stacey-abrams-lawsuit-2018-georgia-governors-election) filed by a voting rights group founded by Abrams.   
  

### Iowa

  
Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds, the first woman elected governor of Iowa, won reelection to a second four-year term. She faced a challenge from Democrat Deidre DeJear, a business owner who is the first Black woman to win a major party’s nomination for statewide office in Iowa. DeJear has never been elected to office, and Republicans hold many levers of political power in the increasingly ruby red state, including control of the legislature.  
  
Reynolds has gained national prominence as one of just three Republican women governors in the country. In March, [she delivered the Republican Party’s rebuttal](https://19thnews.org/2022/03/iowa-governor-kim-reynolds-state-of-the-union-2022-rebuttal/) to Biden’s State of the Union address.  
  
After 2020, Reynolds [expressed public support](https://www.kwqc.com/2020/12/11/gov-reynolds-american-people-deserve-fair-and-transparent-election/) for a Texas lawsuit that would have invalidated election results in several key battleground states.  
  

### Kansas

  
Democratic Gov. [Laura Kelly won reelection](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/laura-kelly-kansas-governor-reelection/) in a conservative-leaning state where Republicans who control the legislature have clashed with her policies. She faced Republican Attorney General Derek Schmidt, a longtime statewide official who has been critical of Kelly’s pandemic response.  
  
Schmidt [was among several elected officials](https://apnews.com/article/election-2020-joe-biden-donald-trump-ken-paxton-kansas-d777e4a19a45f5c95c4b9d78545472b4) who signed their state onto a lawsuit filed in Texas that would have invalidated the 2020 presidential election results, though [he has made private statements](https://kansasreflector.com/2022/03/02/derek-schmidt-embraces-integrity-of-kansas-elections-in-audio-clip-from-gop-forum/) in recent months acknowledging that “Kansas elections are solid.”  
  
While the state generally votes for Republicans, in August, voters [rejected a ballot initiative](https://19thnews.org/2022/08/kansas-abortion-vote-constitutional-protections/) that would have allowed legislators to restrict access to abortion. Kelly campaigned [on issues like the economy](https://19thnews.org/2022/09/kansas-democratic-governor-abortion-restrictions-campaign/) instead of highlighting her role in blocking proposed abortion restrictions that have come up in the legislature.  
  

### Maine

  
Democratic Gov. Janet Mills beat back a challenge from Paul LePage, a two-term former Republican governor who clashed with members of both major parties during his time in office. He notoriously said he was “Donald Trump before Donald Trump.” He has made his criticism of Mills’ response to the pandemic a key issue for his campaign.  
  
LePage initially questioned the results of the 2020 elections, calling it “stolen.” [But he shifted course during an October debate](https://mainebeacon.com/lepage-tries-to-distance-himself-from-trump-distorts-past-stances-in-debate/): “I believe that President Biden won the election.”  
  

### Massachusetts

  
Democratic Attorney General [Maura Healey beat](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/maura-healey-massachusetts-governor/) Trump-backed Republican Geoff Diehl, Decision Desk HQ projects. Kim Driscoll, mayor of the Massachusetts city of Salem, won the lieutenant governor seat alongside Healey — setting up a historic two-women winning ticket.  
  
While Diehl once told Republicans to accept the results of the 2020 election, [he told local press in August](https://www.wgbh.org/news/politics/2022/09/19/diehl-clarifies-stance-on-accepting-result-of-mass-governors-race): “I was wrong initially. It definitely was an election that was stolen from Trump, and it was rigged in a way that should never happen again.”  
  

### Michigan

  
Democratic [Gov. Gretchen Whitmer held off a challenge](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/gretchen-whitmer-michigan-governor-reelection/) from Trump-endorsed Tudor Dixon, who had emerged from a crowded and chaotic Republican field. Whitmer gained national prominence during Trump’s presidency for her public criticism of his policies.  
  
Whitmer made abortion access a key issue for her campaign and tried to legally challenge a dormant 1931 law that nearly bans the procedure.  
  
Dixon, a conservative media personality, [agreed with other candidates during primary debates](https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2022/09/behind-tudor-dixons-shifting-stance-on-election-conspiracy-theories.html) in May and June that widespread voter fraud occurred in Michigan during the 2020 election. But she later declined to answer a question about whether she thought the election was stolen.  
  

### New Mexico

  
Democratic Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham has defeated Mark Ronchettia, a former TV meteorologist who was endorsed by Trump, Decision Desk HQ projects.  
  
Lujan Grisham, who was elected in 2018, is only the third woman of color to ever be elected governor in the country. She outraised all her opponents as she countered criticism about her response to the pandemic — which included extended restrictions on gatherings. Lujan Grisham has defended her decisions, saying they helped save lives in the state. Lujan Grisham also focused on abortion access during her campaign while Ronchetti focused his messaging on the economy and public safety around crime.  
  
Ronchetti told [the](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/gop-gubernatorial-candidate-questionnaires/article_11b0d344-d2d3-11ec-99b4-cfe89c744e15.html)_[Santa Fe New Mexican](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local\_news/gop-gubernatorial-candidate-questionnaires/article\_11b0d344-d2d3-11ec-99b4-cfe89c744e15.html)_[newspaper](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/gop-gubernatorial-candidate-questionnaires/article_11b0d344-d2d3-11ec-99b4-cfe89c744e15.html) earlier this year that he believes Biden is the legitimately elected president; [a spokesperson added](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/ronchetti-under-fire-for-accepting-campaign-contributions-from-fake-presidential-electors/article_819b4d46-45b1-11ed-bcc5-034430ec7784.html) that the Republican candidate does not think the election was stolen. [The nonprofit news outlet Source New Mexico reported in October](https://sourcenm.com/2022/10/05/ronchetti-accepts-donation-from-yet-another-fake-elector/) that Ronchetti has received campaign donations from people connected to a scheme involving fake electors trying to overturn the 2020 presidential results.  
  

### New York

  
Democrat Kathy Hochul won a full term on Tuesday, Decision Desk HQ projects, beating Republican Lee Zeldin.  
  
Hochul became New York’s first woman governor last year when her predecessor, Andrew Cuomo, resigned in disgrace over allegations of sexual misconduct. (He has mostly denied wrongdoing.)  
  
Zeldin, a congressman, highlighted crime statistics and reports of a rocky economy to try to gain footing in a state that leans Democratic. Hochul countered that narrative while emphasizing support for abortion access. Recent polls showed a tightening race.  
  
Zeldin has not made recent public remarks about the 2020 election, but [text messages obtained by the January 6 committee](https://twitter.com/hunterw/status/1582027574309683206?s=20&t=MJdUSGUYh8K84UlFw7ojLQ) show the congressman communicating with former Trump White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows on ideas to challenge the results.  
  

### Oklahoma

  
Republican Gov. Kevin Stitt won reelection. He had faced a challenge from Democrat Joy Hofmeister, the state superintendent of education and a former Republican who switched parties in 2021.  
  
Polling in the final weeks of the race showed it tightening despite the state overwhelmingly voting for Trump in 2020. Several of the state’s largest Native tribes endorsed Hofmeister.  
  

### Oregon

  
A historic [three-woman race is playing out in Oregon](https://19thnews.org/2022/10/oregon-governors-race-kotek-drazan-johnson/), featuring Republican Christine Drazan, Democrat Tina Kotek and third-party candidate Betsy Johnson.  
  
The seat is open — Democratic Gov. Kate Brown is term-limited — creating competitive conditions for any of the candidates to win. The outcome could disrupt a West Coast alliance on abortion access and threaten LGBTQ+ rights within a progressive state. If Kotek wins, she would be one of the country’s first out lesbian governors.  
  
Drazan [has told local press](https://www.oregonlive.com/politics/2022/10/as-republican-christine-drazan-runs-for-oregon-governor-shes-walking-a-careful-line-on-the-ticket-of-a-party-thats-embraced-election-denial-nationally-and-locally.html) that Biden is the president.  
  

### South Dakota

  
Republican Gov. Kristi Noem won reelection to a second term, holding off a challenge from the state House minority leader, Democrat Jamie Smith, in this heavily Republican state.  
  
Noem gained national attention after the start of the pandemic for challenging mitigation measures. More recently, she signed the first anti-trans law of the year and signed an executive order that prohibits mandated teaching of “divisive concepts” in K-12 schools.  
  
Days after the 2020 election, Noem made debunked claims about widespread fraud. She then attended Biden’s inauguration, but later raised doubts about whether the election was fair everywhere.  
  
“We have a result,” [she said in January 2021](https://twitter.com/govkristinoem/status/1354932705138536456?s=20&t=IlG8aDUa0qx5eIscQ3avZw). “We have a president that was elected. He is in office. I am willing to work with him and I believe he is our president of the United States. And I also think there are some reforms that should be pursued in some states where we've seen some places where there wasn't … potential integrity.”

# Record Number of Women Ascend to Governors Offices

## The 2022 midterms were a record-breaking year for women candidates. Several states already have made history with electing their first-time female governor and some are yet to be decided as votes are still being tallied.

Nov. 13, 2022•

Barbara Rodriguez, The 19th

*   [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=314190606794339&display=popup&href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.governing.com%2Fnow%2Frecord-number-of-women-ascend-to-governors-offices)

Sarah Huckabee Sanders speaks Friday, June 11, 2021, during the Indiana GOP Spring Dinner in Indianapolis. Sanders was elected Arkansas' first woman governor on Tuesday, Nov. 8, 2022. 

(Lukas Flippo/IndyStar)

  
_Editor's Note: This article was originally published by [The 19th](https://19thnews.org/2022/05/governors-races-election-2022/)._  
  
At least 11 women are poised to win governorships following Tuesday’s election, a record number. Up until Tuesday, only nine women had served as governor at the same time. Just 45 women have served as governor in American history. But that will change, pending two races in Arizona and Oregon that have only women candidates.  
  
Twenty-five women had been on the ballot Election Day as major-party nominees in 36 governor’s races, another record.  
  
[Maura Healey has won](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/maura-healey-massachusetts-governor/) in Massachusetts, Decision Desk HQ projects, and will be the first out lesbian governor in U.S. history. A number of women Democrats won reelection in competitive races, including [Michigan’s Gretchen Whitmer](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/gretchen-whitmer-michigan-governor-reelection/)and [Kansas’ Laura Kelly](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/laura-kelly-kansas-governor-reelection/).  
  
Here are live results for 14 key governor’s races _The 19th_ is watching:  
  

### Alabama

  
Republican Gov. Kay Ivey, the first woman elected governor of Alabama, won a second four-year term, beating Democrat Yolanda Flowers. Flowers is the first Black woman in the state to win a major party’s nomination for governor. Ivey outraised Flowers throughout the election cycle.  
  
In a campaign ad released in the spring, Ivey claimed “blue state liberals” and others “stole” the 2020 election from Trump. She later told [television station WVTM 13](https://www.wvtm13.com/article/secretary-of-state-said-there-was-no-fraud-in-alabama-s-2020-general-election/39696085#) that she believes Trump won the election.  
  

### Arizona

  
Democrat Katie Hobbs and Republican Kari Lake are in a tight race for an open seat in one of the most closely watched governor’s races in the country.  
  
Hobbs, the current secretary of state, has staked her campaign on protecting elections and democracy. Lake, a former local television anchor, has never been elected to office and has made election denialism a key issue for her campaign. Lake has called [the 2020 election “stolen” and Biden an “illegitimate president.”](https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-biden-doug-ducey-arizona-donald-trump-710d8d35d6414784255fa133e08f190e) If she is elected, she would help oversee elections in a battleground state that is expected to have an outsize role in the 2024 presidential election.  
  

### Arkansas

  
Republican [Sarah Huckabee Sanders has won](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/sarah-huckabee-sanders-arkansas-governor/), Decision Desk HQ projects, making her the first woman to be elected governor of Arkansas.  
  
Sanders has never been elected to office, but she’s gained name recognition as a former White House press secretary for Trump and as the daughter of former Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee.  
  
Sanders, who has highlighted her ties to Trump’s administration on the campaign trail, has expressed some doubt about the 2020 election. She told the [Texarkana Gazette](https://www.texarkanagazette.com/news/2022/may/02/in-race-for-arkansas-governor-gop-hopefuls-differ/) ahead of the May primary: “I don't think we’ll ever know the depths of how much fraud existed.” If Leslie Rutledge — the state’s current attorney general and the Republican nominee for lieutenant governor — is elected alongside Sanders, the two would be among the first women in the country to serve together in the top posts.  
  

### Georgia

  
Democrat Stacey Abrams has lost to incumbent Republican Gov. Brian Kemp, Decision Desk HQ projects. Georgia has also never elected a woman governor.  
  
Abrams emphasized the importance of voting access in her second bid for governor and spent time on the trail highlighting issues including abortion, health care and economic inequality.  
  
Kemp is among the most prominent Republicans to dismiss Trump’s claims about problems with the 2020 election. Abrams has criticized Kemp’s [policies around voting](https://19thnews.org/2022/09/georgia-elections-voter-challenges/), which voting rights groups warn could make it harder for some people to vote.  
  
Abrams [refused to concede](https://19thnews.org/2022/09/stacey-abrams-trump-democracy-big-lie/) after her 2018 loss, claiming that Kemp suppressed voter turnout. Kemp denies this, and in October a judge [tossed a related lawsuit](https://www.axios.com/2022/09/30/stacey-abrams-lawsuit-2018-georgia-governors-election) filed by a voting rights group founded by Abrams.   
  

### Iowa

  
Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds, the first woman elected governor of Iowa, won reelection to a second four-year term. She faced a challenge from Democrat Deidre DeJear, a business owner who is the first Black woman to win a major party’s nomination for statewide office in Iowa. DeJear has never been elected to office, and Republicans hold many levers of political power in the increasingly ruby red state, including control of the legislature.  
  
Reynolds has gained national prominence as one of just three Republican women governors in the country. In March, [she delivered the Republican Party’s rebuttal](https://19thnews.org/2022/03/iowa-governor-kim-reynolds-state-of-the-union-2022-rebuttal/) to Biden’s State of the Union address.  
  
After 2020, Reynolds [expressed public support](https://www.kwqc.com/2020/12/11/gov-reynolds-american-people-deserve-fair-and-transparent-election/) for a Texas lawsuit that would have invalidated election results in several key battleground states.  
  

### Kansas

  
Democratic Gov. [Laura Kelly won reelection](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/laura-kelly-kansas-governor-reelection/) in a conservative-leaning state where Republicans who control the legislature have clashed with her policies. She faced Republican Attorney General Derek Schmidt, a longtime statewide official who has been critical of Kelly’s pandemic response.  
  
Schmidt [was among several elected officials](https://apnews.com/article/election-2020-joe-biden-donald-trump-ken-paxton-kansas-d777e4a19a45f5c95c4b9d78545472b4) who signed their state onto a lawsuit filed in Texas that would have invalidated the 2020 presidential election results, though [he has made private statements](https://kansasreflector.com/2022/03/02/derek-schmidt-embraces-integrity-of-kansas-elections-in-audio-clip-from-gop-forum/) in recent months acknowledging that “Kansas elections are solid.”  
  
While the state generally votes for Republicans, in August, voters [rejected a ballot initiative](https://19thnews.org/2022/08/kansas-abortion-vote-constitutional-protections/) that would have allowed legislators to restrict access to abortion. Kelly campaigned [on issues like the economy](https://19thnews.org/2022/09/kansas-democratic-governor-abortion-restrictions-campaign/) instead of highlighting her role in blocking proposed abortion restrictions that have come up in the legislature.  
  

### Maine

  
Democratic Gov. Janet Mills beat back a challenge from Paul LePage, a two-term former Republican governor who clashed with members of both major parties during his time in office. He notoriously said he was “Donald Trump before Donald Trump.” He has made his criticism of Mills’ response to the pandemic a key issue for his campaign.  
  
LePage initially questioned the results of the 2020 elections, calling it “stolen.” [But he shifted course during an October debate](https://mainebeacon.com/lepage-tries-to-distance-himself-from-trump-distorts-past-stances-in-debate/): “I believe that President Biden won the election.”  
  

### Massachusetts

  
Democratic Attorney General [Maura Healey beat](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/maura-healey-massachusetts-governor/) Trump-backed Republican Geoff Diehl, Decision Desk HQ projects. Kim Driscoll, mayor of the Massachusetts city of Salem, won the lieutenant governor seat alongside Healey — setting up a historic two-women winning ticket.  
  
While Diehl once told Republicans to accept the results of the 2020 election, [he told local press in August](https://www.wgbh.org/news/politics/2022/09/19/diehl-clarifies-stance-on-accepting-result-of-mass-governors-race): “I was wrong initially. It definitely was an election that was stolen from Trump, and it was rigged in a way that should never happen again.”  
  

### Michigan

  
Democratic [Gov. Gretchen Whitmer held off a challenge](https://19thnews.org/2022/11/gretchen-whitmer-michigan-governor-reelection/) from Trump-endorsed Tudor Dixon, who had emerged from a crowded and chaotic Republican field. Whitmer gained national prominence during Trump’s presidency for her public criticism of his policies.  
  
Whitmer made abortion access a key issue for her campaign and tried to legally challenge a dormant 1931 law that nearly bans the procedure.  
  
Dixon, a conservative media personality, [agreed with other candidates during primary debates](https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2022/09/behind-tudor-dixons-shifting-stance-on-election-conspiracy-theories.html) in May and June that widespread voter fraud occurred in Michigan during the 2020 election. But she later declined to answer a question about whether she thought the election was stolen.  
  

### New Mexico

  
Democratic Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham has defeated Mark Ronchettia, a former TV meteorologist who was endorsed by Trump, Decision Desk HQ projects.  
  
Lujan Grisham, who was elected in 2018, is only the third woman of color to ever be elected governor in the country. She outraised all her opponents as she countered criticism about her response to the pandemic — which included extended restrictions on gatherings. Lujan Grisham has defended her decisions, saying they helped save lives in the state. Lujan Grisham also focused on abortion access during her campaign while Ronchetti focused his messaging on the economy and public safety around crime.  
  
Ronchetti told [the](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/gop-gubernatorial-candidate-questionnaires/article_11b0d344-d2d3-11ec-99b4-cfe89c744e15.html)_[Santa Fe New Mexican](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local\_news/gop-gubernatorial-candidate-questionnaires/article\_11b0d344-d2d3-11ec-99b4-cfe89c744e15.html)_[newspaper](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/gop-gubernatorial-candidate-questionnaires/article_11b0d344-d2d3-11ec-99b4-cfe89c744e15.html) earlier this year that he believes Biden is the legitimately elected president; [a spokesperson added](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/ronchetti-under-fire-for-accepting-campaign-contributions-from-fake-presidential-electors/article_819b4d46-45b1-11ed-bcc5-034430ec7784.html) that the Republican candidate does not think the election was stolen. [The nonprofit news outlet Source New Mexico reported in October](https://sourcenm.com/2022/10/05/ronchetti-accepts-donation-from-yet-another-fake-elector/) that Ronchetti has received campaign donations from people connected to a scheme involving fake electors trying to overturn the 2020 presidential results.  
  

### New York

  
Democrat Kathy Hochul won a full term on Tuesday, Decision Desk HQ projects, beating Republican Lee Zeldin.  
  
Hochul became New York’s first woman governor last year when her predecessor, Andrew Cuomo, resigned in disgrace over allegations of sexual misconduct. (He has mostly denied wrongdoing.)  
  
Zeldin, a congressman, highlighted crime statistics and reports of a rocky economy to try to gain footing in a state that leans Democratic. Hochul countered that narrative while emphasizing support for abortion access. Recent polls showed a tightening race.  
  
Zeldin has not made recent public remarks about the 2020 election, but [text messages obtained by the January 6 committee](https://twitter.com/hunterw/status/1582027574309683206?s=20&t=MJdUSGUYh8K84UlFw7ojLQ) show the congressman communicating with former Trump White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows on ideas to challenge the results.  
  

### Oklahoma

  
Republican Gov. Kevin Stitt won reelection. He had faced a challenge from Democrat Joy Hofmeister, the state superintendent of education and a former Republican who switched parties in 2021.  
  
Polling in the final weeks of the race showed it tightening despite the state overwhelmingly voting for Trump in 2020. Several of the state’s largest Native tribes endorsed Hofmeister.  
  

### Oregon

  
A historic [three-woman race is playing out in Oregon](https://19thnews.org/2022/10/oregon-governors-race-kotek-drazan-johnson/), featuring Republican Christine Drazan, Democrat Tina Kotek and third-party candidate Betsy Johnson.  
  
The seat is open — Democratic Gov. Kate Brown is term-limited — creating competitive conditions for any of the candidates to win. The outcome could disrupt a West Coast alliance on abortion access and threaten LGBTQ+ rights within a progressive state. If Kotek wins, she would be one of the country’s first out lesbian governors.  
  
Drazan [has told local press](https://www.oregonlive.com/politics/2022/10/as-republican-christine-drazan-runs-for-oregon-governor-shes-walking-a-careful-line-on-the-ticket-of-a-party-thats-embraced-election-denial-nationally-and-locally.html) that Biden is the president.  
  

### South Dakota

  
Republican Gov. Kristi Noem won reelection to a second term, holding off a challenge from the state House minority leader, Democrat Jamie Smith, in this heavily Republican state.  
  
Noem gained national attention after the start of the pandemic for challenging mitigation measures. More recently, she signed the first anti-trans law of the year and signed an executive order that prohibits mandated teaching of “divisive concepts” in K-12 schools.  
  
Days after the 2020 election, Noem made debunked claims about widespread fraud. She then attended Biden’s inauguration, but later raised doubts about whether the election was fair everywhere.  
  
“We have a result,” [she said in January 2021](https://twitter.com/govkristinoem/status/1354932705138536456?s=20&t=IlG8aDUa0qx5eIscQ3avZw). “We have a president that was elected. He is in office. I am willing to work with him and I believe he is our president of the United States. And I also think there are some reforms that should be pursued in some states where we've seen some places where there wasn't … potential integrity.”

# 19 states have never had a female governor

By [![Image 1: Faith Karimi](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/150511065206-karimi-faith.jpg?q=x_0,y_3,h_1437,w_2554,c_crop/h_270,w_480/c_thumb,g_face,w_50,h_50)](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/faith-karimi)[Faith Karimi](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/faith-karimi)

Updated Aug 24, 2021

Updated Aug 24, 2021, 8:26 AM ET

PUBLISHED Aug 24, 2021, 8:25 AM ET

![Image 2: Kathy Hochul, right, is sworn in as New York state's governor by Court of Appeals Chief Judge Janet DiFiore on a Bible held by her husband Bill Hochul. ](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210824062054-01-kathy-hochul-swearing-in-0824.jpg?q=w_2730,h_1921,x_0,y_0,c_fill/w_860)

Kathy Hochul, right, is sworn in as New York state's governor by Court of Appeals Chief Judge Janet DiFiore on a Bible held by her husband Bill Hochul. 

Hans Pennink/Pool/Getty Images

When she was [sworn in shortly after midnight](http://www.cnn.com/2021/08/23/politics/kathy-hochul-new-york-governor/index.html), Democrat Kathy Hochul became the first female governor in New York state history.

She also became one of [nine women governors](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/women-statewide-elective-executive-office-2021) currently serving in the US, tying a record high.

Progress, right?

Ad Feedback

Yes. But when you examine the track record of women in governors’ mansions, it’s clear that gender equality has a long way to go.

Hochul is only [the 45th female governor](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/sites/default/files/resources/press-advisory-ny-governor-transition.pdf) in the 245-year history of the US, according to data by the Center for American Women and Politics (CAWP) at Rutgers University.

With the addition of New York, 31 states have now had a woman governor. Nineteen states have not.

While [27% of seats in the current Congress are held by women](https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2021/01/15/a-record-number-of-women-are-serving-in-the-117th-congress/) – the highest percentage in history – just 18% of the nation’s governors are women.

Experts say women have a tougher time getting elected as governors for several reasons.

“The biggest one is the perception that the leadership qualities that one needs to be a governor (or a President) are not ones that women possess,” said Debbie Walsh, CAWP’s director. “The image of a governor (or President) is still male with gendered stereotypes of how men lead – decisive, authoritative, the place where the buck stops.”

The notion that women tend to work collaboratively has helped them get elected as legislators on the state or federal level, but that stereotype has worked against them with elected executive leadership, Walsh said.

Anthony Behar/Sipa USA/AP How NY's first female governor will lead the state](https://www.cnn.com/2021/08/22/opinions/kathy-hochul-first-woman-governor-new-york-quinn/index.html)

Party leaders also have traditionally been men who have recruited gubernatorial candidates from their own social and political networks, said Kelly Dittmar, an associate professor of political science at Rutgers University.

Gubernatorial vacancies do not arise often, and male gatekeepers have long kept the lists of who is next in line, forcing women candidates to either gain the blessing of these leaders or challenge them in primaries, Dittmar added.

“One of the advantages that Kathy Hochul will have coming in is that she will have 18 months to prove that her style of leadership is effective and show voters a different image of who can be a governor,” Walsh said. “We have seen this as a successful model for other women governors.”

## **Little-known facts about female governors**

*    The list of female governors includes [27 Democrats and 18 Republicans](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/history-women-governors). (Women also have served as governors in the US territories of Guam and Puerto Rico). 

![Image 4: Governor Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210823142326-01-female-governors-ross.jpg?q=w_2500,h_3084,x_0,y_0,c_fill/w_632)

Governor Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming.

Bettmann/Getty Images

*    Wyoming was the first state with a female governor. Gov. Nellie Tayloe Ross won a special election in 1925 to replace her husband after he died. 

*    Arizona has had four female governors – the most of any state. They have been from both major parties, and three of them served consecutive terms. 
*    Of the 45 female governors, 30 were first elected in their own right; three replaced their husbands and 12, including Hochul, became governor by constitutional succession. 

![Image 5: Ella T. Grasso, Governor of Connecticut, in her office in an undated photo.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210823144507-02-female-governors-grasso.jpg?q=w_2500,h_1695,x_0,y_0,c_fill/w_632)

Ella T. Grasso, Governor of Connecticut, in her office in an undated photo.

Bettman/Getty Images

*    In 1975 Connecticut’s Ella Grasso became the first woman elected governor in her own right. 
*    The current record of nine women serving as governors was also equaled in 2004, 2007 and 2019. 

*    Three women of color have served as governors: Republican Nikki Haley of South Carolina, Republican Susana Martinez of New Mexico, and Democrat Michelle Lujan Grisham of New Mexico. [No Black or Native American women](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/sites/default/files/resources/press-advisory-ny-governor-transition.pdf) have ever served as governor. 

## **These states have never had a female governor**

The nine states which currently have female governors: Oregon, New York, Alabama, Kansas, New Mexico, Maine, South Dakota, Iowa and Michigan.

These 19 states [have only had male governors](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/sites/default/files/resources/press-advisory-ny-governor-transition.pdf):

*    Arkansas 

*    California 

*    Colorado 

*    Florida

*    Wisconsin 

*    West Virginia

# 19 states have never had a female governor

By [![Image 1: Faith Karimi](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/150511065206-karimi-faith.jpg?q=x_0,y_3,h_1437,w_2554,c_crop/h_270,w_480/c_thumb,g_face,w_50,h_50)](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/faith-karimi)[Faith Karimi](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/faith-karimi)

Updated Aug 24, 2021

 Link Copied! 

![Image 2: Kathy Hochul, right, is sworn in as New York state's governor by Court of Appeals Chief Judge Janet DiFiore on a Bible held by her husband Bill Hochul. ](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210824062054-01-kathy-hochul-swearing-in-0824.jpg?q=w_2730,h_1921,x_0,y_0,c_fill/w_860)

Kathy Hochul, right, is sworn in as New York state's governor by Court of Appeals Chief Judge Janet DiFiore on a Bible held by her husband Bill Hochul. 

Hans Pennink/Pool/Getty Images

When she was [sworn in shortly after midnight](http://www.cnn.com/2021/08/23/politics/kathy-hochul-new-york-governor/index.html), Democrat Kathy Hochul became the first female governor in New York state history.

She also became one of [nine women governors](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/women-statewide-elective-executive-office-2021) currently serving in the US, tying a record high.

Progress, right?

Ad Feedback

Yes. But when you examine the track record of women in governors’ mansions, it’s clear that gender equality has a long way to go.

Hochul is only [the 45th female governor](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/sites/default/files/resources/press-advisory-ny-governor-transition.pdf) in the 245-year history of the US, according to data by the Center for American Women and Politics (CAWP) at Rutgers University.

With the addition of New York, 31 states have now had a woman governor. Nineteen states have not.

While [27% of seats in the current Congress are held by women](https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2021/01/15/a-record-number-of-women-are-serving-in-the-117th-congress/) – the highest percentage in history – just 18% of the nation’s governors are women.

Experts say women have a tougher time getting elected as governors for several reasons.

“The biggest one is the perception that the leadership qualities that one needs to be a governor (or a President) are not ones that women possess,” said Debbie Walsh, CAWP’s director. “The image of a governor (or President) is still male with gendered stereotypes of how men lead – decisive, authoritative, the place where the buck stops.”

The notion that women tend to work collaboratively has helped them get elected as legislators on the state or federal level, but that stereotype has worked against them with elected executive leadership, Walsh said.

Governor Kathy Hochul will become the first female Governor of New York State when she takes over for Governor Andrew Cuomo, who announced his resignation after a report by New York State Attorney General Letitia James claims the Governor had sexually harassed 11 women. ](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210811144518-01-kathy-hochul-0811.jpg?q=x_4,y_59,h_2246,w_3991,c_crop/h_720,w_1280/w_256) Lt. Governor Kathy Hochul speaks at a press conference at the New York State Capital in Albany New York, NY on August 11, 2021. Lt. Governor Kathy Hochul will become the first female Governor of New York State when she takes over for Governor Andrew Cuomo, who announced his resignation after a report by New York State Attorney General Letitia James claims the Governor had sexually harassed 11 women. Anthony Behar/Sipa USA/AP How NY's first female governor will lead the state](https://www.cnn.com/2021/08/22/opinions/kathy-hochul-first-woman-governor-new-york-quinn/index.html)

Party leaders also have traditionally been men who have recruited gubernatorial candidates from their own social and political networks, said Kelly Dittmar, an associate professor of political science at Rutgers University.

Gubernatorial vacancies do not arise often, and male gatekeepers have long kept the lists of who is next in line, forcing women candidates to either gain the blessing of these leaders or challenge them in primaries, Dittmar added.

“One of the advantages that Kathy Hochul will have coming in is that she will have 18 months to prove that her style of leadership is effective and show voters a different image of who can be a governor,” Walsh said. “We have seen this as a successful model for other women governors.”

## **Little-known facts about female governors**

*    The list of female governors includes [27 Democrats and 18 Republicans](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/history-women-governors). (Women also have served as governors in the US territories of Guam and Puerto Rico). 

![Image 4: Governor Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210823142326-01-female-governors-ross.jpg?q=w_2500,h_3084,x_0,y_0,c_fill/w_632)

Governor Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming.

Bettmann/Getty Images

*    Wyoming was the first state with a female governor. Gov. Nellie Tayloe Ross won a special election in 1925 to replace her husband after he died. 

*    Arizona has had four female governors – the most of any state. They have been from both major parties, and three of them served consecutive terms. 
*    Of the 45 female governors, 30 were first elected in their own right; three replaced their husbands and 12, including Hochul, became governor by constitutional succession. 

![Image 5: Ella T. Grasso, Governor of Connecticut, in her office in an undated photo.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/210823144507-02-female-governors-grasso.jpg?q=w_2500,h_1695,x_0,y_0,c_fill/w_632)

Ella T. Grasso, Governor of Connecticut, in her office in an undated photo.

Bettman/Getty Images

*    In 1975 Connecticut’s Ella Grasso became the first woman elected governor in her own right. 
*    The current record of nine women serving as governors was also equaled in 2004, 2007 and 2019.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

Male

Female

As of 2026, 53 women have served as [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States) "Governor (United States)") of a [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), four as governor of an [unincorporated U.S. territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_territories_of_the_United_States "Unincorporated territories of the United States"), and two as [mayor of the District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_the_District_of_Columbia "Mayor of the District of Columbia"). In January 2026, women have been serving as governor in 14 U.S. states, as mayor of the District of Columbia, and as territorial governors of [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam") and [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"). Of the current female state governors, ten are [Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") and four are [Republicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). [Madeleine Kunin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeleine_Kunin "Madeleine Kunin") is the oldest living former female governor at 92.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

See also: [List of the first women holders of political offices in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_first_women_holders_of_political_offices_in_the_United_States "List of the first women holders of political offices in the United States")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Female_governors.svg/250px-Female_governors.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Female_governors.svg)

The first woman to act as governor was [Carolyn B. Shelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_B._Shelton "Carolyn B. Shelton"), who served as Acting Governor of Oregon for one weekend from 9 a.m. on February 27, through 10 a.m. on March 1, 1909. The outgoing governor, [George Earle Chamberlain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_E._Chamberlain "George E. Chamberlain"), had been elected to the U.S. Senate and had to leave for Washington, D.C., before his term ended; the incoming governor, [Frank W. Benson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_W._Benson_(politician) "Frank W. Benson (politician)"), had become ill and could not assume office early. Chamberlain left Shelton, his secretary, in charge for the weekend.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-1)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] It was another three and a half years before women were allowed to vote in Oregon.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-Oregon_Historical_Quarterly-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-4)

The first female acting governor to be entrusted with substantial duties while in office was [Soledad Chávez de Chacón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soledad_Chac%C3%B3n "Soledad Chacón"), who held the powers and duties of [Governor of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Mexico "Governor of New Mexico") for two weeks in 1924 while Governor [James F. Hinkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_F._Hinkle "James F. Hinkle") attended the Democratic Convention in New York. Lieutenant Governor [José A. Baca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_A._Baca "José A. Baca") had died in May, so Chacón, the Secretary of State, filled the position. Chacón said that she believed that her 1924 elevation was the first time in the United States that a woman had been called on to assume the responsibilities of the governor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-AJ20100824-5)

The first woman to assume office as governor pursuant to a special election was [Nellie Tayloe Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellie_Tayloe_Ross "Nellie Tayloe Ross") of [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming"), who was elected on November 4, 1924, following the death of her husband and former governor, [William B. Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_B._Ross "William B. Ross"), and was sworn in on January 5, 1925.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-6) Wyoming was the first state to provide women's suffrage[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-7) after [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") had abolished it in 1807. [Miriam A. Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miriam_A._Ferguson "Miriam A. Ferguson") of [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas") won the general election of November 4, 1924, and was sworn in on January 20, 1925. Her husband, former governor [James Edward Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_E._Ferguson "James E. Ferguson"), had been [impeached](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment "Impeachment") and removed from office in 1917.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-8) The first woman elected governor who was not the wife or widow of a former state governor was [Ella T. Grasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Grasso "Ella Grasso") of [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"), elected in 1974 and sworn in on January 8, 1975.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-9)[Kay Ivey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Ivey "Kay Ivey") of [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"), is the longest-serving female governor in the nation. She is currently serving having been first elected in 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-10)

To date, no woman has ever changed parties during her gubernatorial term or has been elected as a [third-party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_party_(U.S._politics) "Third party (U.S. politics)") member or an independent.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Demographics")]

As of 2026, [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"), [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona"), [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"), [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire"), [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), and [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico") are the only states to have elected women as governors from both major parties. Arizona was the first state where a woman followed another woman as governor (they were from different parties). Arizona has also had the most with five, and is the first state to have three consecutive women to serve as governor.

A record 14 out of 50 state governorships were held by women following [Mikie Sherrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikie_Sherrill "Mikie Sherrill")'s inauguration as the [Governor of New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Jersey "Governor of New Jersey") on January 20, 2026. This record of 14 was briefly matched for less than two weeks in January 2025 following the inauguration of [Kelly Ayotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Ayotte "Kelly Ayotte") of [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire") on January 9 but prior to the departure of [Bethany Hall-Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethany_Hall-Long "Bethany Hall-Long") of [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware") on January 21.

Also, 19 states have never elected a female governor: [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [Idaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho "Idaho"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana "Indiana"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota"), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"), [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada"), [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota"), [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"), [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), and [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin"). Two states (Mississippi and Utah) have never seen a major party nominate a woman in a gubernatorial election, although one woman, [Olene Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olene_Walker "Olene Walker"), had assumed the office of Governor of Utah from 2003 to 2005 after previous governor, [Mike Leavitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Leavitt "Mike Leavitt"), resigned.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-11)

Three women of color have been state governors: [Susana Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susana_Martinez "Susana Martinez") and [Michelle Lujan Grisham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Lujan_Grisham "Michelle Lujan Grisham") of New Mexico (both Hispanic) and [Nikki Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Haley "Nikki Haley") of South Carolina (Indian-American). Martinez and Haley are both Republican; Lujan Grisham is a Democrat. Additionally, all six women who governed an insular area have been of an ethnic minority group: [Sharon Pratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Pratt "Sharon Pratt") and [Muriel Bowser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muriel_Bowser "Muriel Bowser") of Washington, D.C. (both African-American), [Sila María Calderón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sila_Mar%C3%ADa_Calder%C3%B3n "Sila María Calderón"), [Wanda Vázquez Garced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanda_V%C3%A1zquez_Garced "Wanda Vázquez Garced") and [Jenniffer González-Colón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenniffer_Gonz%C3%A1lez-Col%C3%B3n "Jenniffer González-Colón") of Puerto Rico (all Hispanic), and [Lou Leon Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Leon_Guerrero "Lou Leon Guerrero") of Guam (Pacific Islander). Pratt, Bowser, Calderón, and Guerrero are Democrats, while Vázquez Garced and Gonzalez-Colon are Republicans.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

As of 2026, 53 women have served as [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_(United_States) "Governor (United States)") of a [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), four as governor of an [unincorporated U.S. territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_territories_of_the_United_States "Unincorporated territories of the United States"), and two as [mayor of the District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_the_District_of_Columbia "Mayor of the District of Columbia"). In January 2026, women have been serving as governor in 14 U.S. states, as mayor of the District of Columbia, and as territorial governors of [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam") and [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"). Of the current female state governors, ten are [Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") and four are [Republicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). [Madeleine Kunin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeleine_Kunin "Madeleine Kunin") is the oldest living former female governor at 92.

## History

The first woman to act as governor was [Carolyn B. Shelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_B._Shelton "Carolyn B. Shelton"), who served as Acting Governor of Oregon for one weekend from 9 a.m. on February 27, through 10 a.m. on March 1, 1909. The outgoing governor, [George Earle Chamberlain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_E._Chamberlain "George E. Chamberlain"), had been elected to the U.S. Senate and had to leave for Washington, D.C., before his term ended; the incoming governor, [Frank W. Benson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_W._Benson_(politician) "Frank W. Benson (politician)"), had become ill and could not assume office early. Chamberlain left Shelton, his secretary, in charge for the weekend.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-1)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] It was another three and a half years before women were allowed to vote in Oregon.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-Oregon_Historical_Quarterly-2)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-4)

The first female acting governor to be entrusted with substantial duties while in office was [Soledad Chávez de Chacón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soledad_Chac%C3%B3n "Soledad Chacón"), who held the powers and duties of [Governor of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Mexico "Governor of New Mexico") for two weeks in 1924 while Governor [James F. Hinkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_F._Hinkle "James F. Hinkle") attended the Democratic Convention in New York. Lieutenant Governor [José A. Baca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_A._Baca "José A. Baca") had died in May, so Chacón, the Secretary of State, filled the position. Chacón said that she believed that her 1924 elevation was the first time in the United States that a woman had been called on to assume the responsibilities of the governor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-AJ20100824-5)

The first woman to assume office as governor pursuant to a special election was [Nellie Tayloe Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellie_Tayloe_Ross "Nellie Tayloe Ross") of [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming"), who was elected on November 4, 1924, following the death of her husband and former governor, [William B. Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_B._Ross "William B. Ross"), and was sworn in on January 5, 1925.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-6) Wyoming was the first state to provide women's suffrage[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-7) after [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") had abolished it in 1807. [Miriam A. Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miriam_A._Ferguson "Miriam A. Ferguson") of [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas") won the general election of November 4, 1924, and was sworn in on January 20, 1925. Her husband, former governor [James Edward Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_E._Ferguson "James E. Ferguson"), had been [impeached](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment "Impeachment") and removed from office in 1917.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-8) The first woman elected governor who was not the wife or widow of a former state governor was [Ella T. Grasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Grasso "Ella Grasso") of [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"), elected in 1974 and sworn in on January 8, 1975.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-9)[Kay Ivey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Ivey "Kay Ivey") of [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"), is the longest-serving female governor in the nation. She is currently serving having been first elected in 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-10)

To date, no woman has ever changed parties during her gubernatorial term or has been elected as a [third-party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_party_(U.S._politics) "Third party (U.S. politics)") member or an independent.

## Demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Demographics")]

As of 2026, [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama"), [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona"), [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"), [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire"), [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), and [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico") are the only states to have elected women as governors from both major parties. Arizona was the first state where a woman followed another woman as governor (they were from different parties). Arizona has also had the most with five, and is the first state to have three consecutive women to serve as governor.

A record 14 out of 50 state governorships were held by women following [Mikie Sherrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikie_Sherrill "Mikie Sherrill")'s inauguration as the [Governor of New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_Jersey "Governor of New Jersey") on January 20, 2026. This record of 14 was briefly matched for less than two weeks in January 2025 following the inauguration of [Kelly Ayotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Ayotte "Kelly Ayotte") of [New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire "New Hampshire") on January 9 but prior to the departure of [Bethany Hall-Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethany_Hall-Long "Bethany Hall-Long") of [Delaware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware "Delaware") on January 21.

Also, 19 states have never elected a female governor: [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)"), [Idaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho "Idaho"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana "Indiana"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota"), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"), [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada"), [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota"), [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"), [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), and [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin"). Two states (Mississippi and Utah) have never seen a major party nominate a woman in a gubernatorial election, although one woman, [Olene Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olene_Walker "Olene Walker"), had assumed the office of Governor of Utah from 2003 to 2005 after previous governor, [Mike Leavitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Leavitt "Mike Leavitt"), resigned.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_female_governors_in_the_United_States#cite_note-11)

Three women of color have been state governors: [Susana Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susana_Martinez "Susana Martinez") and [Michelle Lujan Grisham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Lujan_Grisham "Michelle Lujan Grisham") of New Mexico (both Hispanic) and [Nikki Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Haley "Nikki Haley") of South Carolina (Indian-American). Martinez and Haley are both Republican; Lujan Grisham is a Democrat. Additionally, all six women who governed an insular area have been of an ethnic minority group: [Sharon Pratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Pratt "Sharon Pratt") and [Muriel Bowser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muriel_Bowser "Muriel Bowser") of Washington, D.C. (both African-American), [Sila María Calderón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sila_Mar%C3%ADa_Calder%C3%B3n "Sila María Calderón"), [Wanda Vázquez Garced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanda_V%C3%A1zquez_Garced "Wanda Vázquez Garced") and [Jenniffer González-Colón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenniffer_Gonz%C3%A1lez-Col%C3%B3n "Jenniffer González-Colón") of Puerto Rico (all Hispanic), and [Lou Leon Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Leon_Guerrero "Lou Leon Guerrero") of Guam (Pacific Islander). Pratt, Bowser, Calderón, and Guerrero are Democrats, while Vázquez Garced and Gonzalez-Colon are Republicans.

# 17 states haven’t had a female U.S. senator, and 18 haven’t had a woman governor

[](https://www.pewresearch.org/?p=191228)*   X

By[Katherine Schaeffer](https://www.pewresearch.org/staff/katherine-schaeffer/)

If Kamala Harris wins the presidency this November, she will be the first woman ever elected to the highest political office of the United States.

There could also be similar firsts in political contests around the country: Five races for U.S. Senate and two for governor feature a major-party nominee who, if elected, would be the first woman in their state to hold the office. And in Minnesota, a woman will ascend to the governorship for the first time if current Gov. Tim Walz is elected as Harris’ vice president.

How we did this

If elected, Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris would be the first woman in the top political office in the United States. We conducted this analysis to determine how many Senate and governor’s races could result in similar firsts.

For this analysis, we used data from[U.S. Senate historical records](https://www.senate.gov/senators/ListofWomenSenators.htm), the [Rutgers University Center for American Women and Politics](https://cawp.rutgers.edu/) and recent news reports.

[![Image 3: A map showing that 17 states have never been represented by a woman in the U.S. Senate.](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2024/10/SR_24.10.31_women-leaders_1.png?w=640)](https://www.pewresearch.org/?attachment_id=191234)
Overall, 17 states have never had a female senator, according to a Pew Research Center analysis of Senate historical records. This fall, Senate races in Delaware, Indiana, New Mexico, Rhode Island and Utah each feature a woman nominee who could become the state’s first.

Three of these candidates ([Lisa Blunt Rochester](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/10/05/lisa-blunt-rochester-black-woman-senate/) of Delaware, [Valerie McCray](https://www.wbaa.org/local-news/2024-05-07/valerie-mccray-wins-democratic-u-s-senate-primary-making-indiana-history) of Indiana and [Caroline Gleich](https://www.deseret.com/utah/2024/08/27/caroline-gleich-running-to-replace-mitt-romney-utah-senate/) of Utah) are Democrats, and two ([Nella Domenici](https://www.aol.com/heinrich-battles-domenici-hold-onto-233400342.html) of New Mexico and [Patricia Morgan](https://rhodeislandcurrent.com/2024/09/24/name-recognition-remains-a-challenge-for-morgans-u-s-senate-bid/) of Rhode Island) are Republicans.

Blunt Rochester and McCray would also be the first Black senators to represent their respective states.

[![Image 4: A map showing that women have held governships in about two-thirds of states.](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2024/10/SR_24.10.31_women-leaders_2.png?w=640)](https://www.pewresearch.org/?attachment_id=191233)
Among the 18 states that have never had a woman governor, two – Indiana and Missouri – have a woman on the ballot in this year’s general election. [Jennifer McCormick](https://indianacapitalchronicle.com/2024/10/07/democrat-jennifer-mccormick-runs-on-optimism-embracing-republican-past/) of Indiana and [Crystal Quade](https://missouriindependent.com/2024/08/06/crystal-quade-captures-democratic-nomination-for-missouri-governor/) of Missouri are both Democratic nominees.

And in Minnesota, Lt. Gov. [Peggy Flanagan](https://www.npr.org/2024/08/23/nx-s1-5078569/peggy-flanagan-minnesota-indigenous-walz-harris-trump-election) will take over as governor if Walz is elected vice president. That would make her the first woman and the first Native American person to hold the office.

Five states have not had a woman senator _or_ a woman governor: Colorado, Idaho, Indiana, Pennsylvania and Virginia.

Women have served in numerous statewide [executive and legislative offices](https://cawpdata.rutgers.edu/women-elected-officials/position?current=2&yearend_filter=All&level%5B%5D=Statewide&items_per_page=50) over the decades, including in all the states where they have not yet held Senate seats or governorships. And every state has [sent at least one woman](https://www.npr.org/2022/11/08/1134352130/vermont-balint-election-day-results-2022) to either the U.S. House of Representatives or the Senate.

#### Women in the 118th Senate

In the current Congress, women hold 25 of 100 Senate seats – [a record high](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/01/03/118th-congress-has-a-record-number-of-women/). They represent a total of 21 states. In Minnesota, Nevada, New Hampshire and Washington, both senators are women.

Fourteen of the 25 current senators are the first women to represent their state in the Senate. Their tenures vary: Washington Democrat [Patty Murray](https://awpc.cattcenter.iastate.edu/directory/patty-murray/) has served in the Senate since 1993, whereas Wyoming Republican [Cynthia Lummis](https://www.wyomingpublicmedia.org/politics/2020-11-03/cynthia-lummis-becomes-first-woman-to-win-wyoming-senate-seat) took office in 2021.

Fifteen current women senators are Democrats, nine are Republicans and one (Kyrsten Sinema of Arizona) is an independent. Looking at the Senate as a whole, women make up a larger share of the Democratic caucus (31%) than the Republican caucus (18%).

#### A century in the Senate

Women have served in the Senate for over a century. In 1922, [Rebecca Latimer Felton](http://www.georgiaencyclopedia.org/articles/history-archaeology/rebecca-latimer-felton-1835-1930), a suffragist from Georgia, became the first woman senator. She was appointed to a vacant seat and served for just one day.

[![Image 5: An area chart showing that 60 women have been U.S. senators.](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2024/10/SR_24.10.31_women-leaders_4.png?w=640)](https://www.pewresearch.org/?attachment_id=191235)
Since then, a total of 60 women have represented 33 states in the Senate, and most of them have served in recent decades. About three-quarters (46) first took office after 1980.

A little over half (19) of the states that have ever been represented by a woman in the Senate have sent more than one.

Four women have represented California in the Senate, the most from any state. In addition to Harris, who [represented the state](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/08/22/us/politics/kamala-harris-senate.html) from 2017 to 2021, this group includes two long-serving senators. Democrat [Dianne Feinstein](https://apnews.com/article/dianne-feinstein-dead-c831f3228ac44faa9653234570bb8ce9) took office in 1992 and served until her death in 2023, and [Barbara Boxer](https://bioguide.congress.gov/search/bio/B000711), also a Democrat, was in office from 1993 to 2017.

Alabama, Louisiana, Maine, Minnesota, Nebraska and New Hampshire have each sent three women to the Senate.

**_Related:_**[_22 states have ever elected a Black woman to Congress_](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/02/16/22-states-have-ever-elected-a-black-woman-to-congress/)

#### Women in the governor’s mansion

[![Image 6: An area chart showing that 49 women have been U.S. governors.](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2024/10/SR_24.10.31_women-leaders_3.png?w=640)](https://www.pewresearch.org/?attachment_id=191229)
Overall, 49 women have held the governorship in 32 states since 1925, when two women took the oath of office for the first time.

That year, [Nellie Tayloe Ross](https://www.nga.org/governor/nellie-tayloe-ross/) of Wyoming was nominated in a special election and won the governorship following the death of her husband, Gov. William Ross. [Miriam “Ma” Ferguson](https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/archive/html/exec/governors/15.html) of Texas, the first woman ever chosen for the office in a general election, was sworn in just 15 days later.

Women currently serve as governors in 12 states. Eight are Democrats and four are Republicans.

Five of the current governors are the first women elected in their state: Democrats Janet Mills of Maine and Kathy Hochul of New York; and Republicans Kim Reynolds of Iowa, Kristi Noem of South Dakota and Sarah Huckabee Sanders of Arkansas.

In Arizona, five women have held the governorship since 1988 – by far the most from any state. In fact, three women served consecutively over a 17-year stretch, from Republican [Jane Hull’s](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/jane-hull-first-woman-elected-arizona-governor-dies-at-84) ascension in 1997 until Republican [Jan Brewer](https://www.nga.org/governor/jan-brewer/) left office in 2015.

_CORRECTION (Nov. 1, 2024): This analysis has been updated to indicate that every state has been represented by a woman in either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate._

# 17 states haven’t had a female U.S. senator, and 18 haven’t had a woman governor

[](https://www.pewresearch.org/?p=191228)*   X
